title: UConn's First Big East Tournament Crown
dek: Down 10-0 to top-seeded Syracuse, UConn rallied behind its pressing defense and 58 points from three guards to win 78-75 — its first Big East tournament title.

setup.text: The Big East's coaches picked UConn eighth before the season, after leading scorer Cliff Robinson graduated. Instead the Huskies tied Syracuse for the regular-season title, and Jim Calhoun was voted the league's coach of the year.

Seeded second and ranked eighth in the country, UConn routed Seton Hall 76-58 and came from 9 points down in the second half to beat No. 5 Georgetown 65-60, reaching the final for the first time in the league's 11 years.
Syracuse, the top seed and No. 4 in the country, was in its eighth Big East final. The teams had split during the season: UConn won 70-59 in Hartford, and Syracuse won 90-86 at home before 32,820.

UConn would be thin inside. Center Rod Sellers had twisted his injured left knee less than two minutes into the Georgetown game, which left Toraino Walker — a 6-foot-6 freshman who had played 65 minutes in the entire Big East regular season — to help handle Derrick Coleman, the conference's player of the year.

game.text: Syracuse scored the first 10 points while UConn came up empty on nine trips down the floor, and Calhoun called time to tell his players they were too good to play this poorly. Smith's 5-foot jumper and free throw finally got UConn on the board.
About six minutes in, Coleman dunked, traded high-fives and made the free throw for a 17-5 lead, and Syracuse still led 25-14 with 10:23 left in the half.

Then UConn's press took over. Syracuse turned the ball over 14 times in the first half and missed eight of 13 free throws, and from 17-5 down UConn went on a 37-16 run. Walker, playing through back spasms, scored 10 of his 11 points in the half: his basket tied it 29-29 with 5:49 left, his free throws gave UConn its first lead, and another basket made it 35-29 with 3:29 left.
Tate George's two free throws with 36.2 seconds left made it 42-33, and UConn led 42-35 at halftime. A Smith 3-pointer to start the second half pushed the lead to 10.

sequence.text: Syracuse chips away at a 49-40 deficit; a basket by Tony Scott, who scores all 12 of his points after halftime, makes it 49-47.
Stephen Thompson's bank shot ties it at 57 with about eight and a half minutes left. John Gwynn answers with a deep 3-pointer from the left wing, fouled by Thompson as he shoots.
Coleman dunks to tie it again.
Nadav Henefeld's floater in the lane puts UConn ahead for good.
Gwynn drives on Dave Johnson and, fouled on his right side, flips a left-handed hook over his head, off the glass and in. The free throw makes it a four-point game.
A Scott 3-pointer has cut it to three. Smith's next basket is wiped out when Scott draws the offensive foul.
Scott is called for traveling, and Smith makes a free throw.
George, the senior who told Calhoun he wanted the ball, makes two free throws.
Syracuse gets within four, according to the CBS score graphic.

George makes his last four free throws too — six straight in the final 30 seconds, 8 for 8 for the game — and raises a finger after the last one, with 7 seconds left. UConn wins 78-75, and fans flood the floor for seven minutes.

quotes.text: We are too good . . . and have come too far to play this poorly.
quotes.when: postgame, recalling what he told the team at 10-0

quotes.text: It was time for another team to go ahead and win it. It gets tiring seeing the same teams win it every year.
We've come so far. At times those four-mile runs seemed ludicrous. It seems like it's paying off now.
They can beat anybody. They got a whole lot better team than people think.

aftermath.text: About an hour and a half later, the NCAA made UConn the No. 1 seed in the East and sent it to the Hartford Civic Center to open against 16th-seeded Boston University.

Connecticut went UConn-crazy. A Danbury radio station recorded a UConn fight song and sold it on cassette, scalpers in Hartford were asking $100 or more for the few remaining tournament tickets, and at Storrs, where three sanctioned bonfires had been held in recent days, nine students faced disciplinary charges over a post-game blaze that consumed a dorm couch and two chairs.

In Hartford, UConn beat Boston University 76-52 and California 74-54. At East Rutherford, N.J., it beat Clemson 71-70 in the regional semifinal, then lost to Duke 79-78 in overtime in the regional final, finishing 31-6.

legacy.text: No team other than Georgetown, St. John's or Syracuse had won the Big East tournament before; Georgetown had six titles, and Syracuse and St. John's two each.
It was the first of the eight Big East tournament championships listed in UConn's 2026-27 record book: 1990, 1996, 1998, 1999, 2002, 2004, 2011 and 2024.

source.paper: Manchester Herald (Manchester, Conn.), Associated Press box score
source.printed_page: Scoreboard, p. 12 (PDF page 7 is a two-page spread)
source.method: Transcribed from a 600-dpi render of the page image; OCR ignored where it garbled digits. Every player line, both team totals and the score were re-added and match.

box.format: Standard AP agate box: per-player FG-FGA, FT-FTA and points, plus team 3-point, rebound, assist and foul totals with leaders. No minutes, per-player rebounds or assists, steals, turnovers or blocks.

players.name: Rod Sellers
players.notes: Played 2 minutes on an injured left knee (NYT; Manchester Herald).

players.name: Toraino Walker
players.notes: 24 minutes and 6 rebounds (Manchester Herald); 4 steals (NYT). The box lists him as UConn's rebound leader with 6.

notes: Printed exactly: 'Halftime—Connecticut 42, Syracuse 35. 3-point goals—Connecticut 3-8 (Smith 2-3, Gwynn 1-2, Burrell 0-1, Henefeld 0-2), Syracuse 6-14 (Scott 3-5, Owens 1-2, Johnson 1-2, Edwards 1-4, Thompson 0-1). Fouled out—None. Rebounds—Connecticut 29 (Walker 6), Syracuse 33 (Coleman 10). Assists—Connecticut 13 (DePriest, George, Burrell 3), Syracuse 19 (Owens 8). Total fouls—Connecticut 22, Syracuse 22. A—18,212.'
The box prints surnames only; first names are from the site roster (UConn) and orangehoops.org's 1989-90 Syracuse roster.

'starter' follows the AP convention of listing the five starters first. Cyrulik as a starter is corroborated by the LA Times ('starter Dan Cyrulik') and Syracuse's starters by orangehoops.org. UConn's record book instead lists Sellers as a starter (see conflicts).
Not in the box but reported: Syracuse committed 20 turnovers, 13 on UConn steals (Washington Post; NYT says Walker had 4 of UConn's 13 steals).

conflicts.ours: UConn Record Book (the site's source), 'All-time Big East Tournament results and starters': Scott Burrell, Nadav Henefeld, Rod Sellers, Tate George, Chris Smith
conflicts.source_says: The AP box lists Cyrulik among the first five and Sellers as a reserve; the LA Times calls Cyrulik the 'starter' Coleman overpowered; the NYT (March 11) said Sellers was not expected to play, and he played 2 minutes

unsure: CBS announcers not identified: the broadcast shows two announcers on camera (~80 s and ~5770 s) but I found no name graphic in sampled frames.

Smith's free throw at 0:43.5: the Washington Post says he made the front end of a one-and-one 'with 43.5 seconds left'; the Herald says Scott was called for traveling with 43.5 left and then Smith made one. The beat uses 0:43.5 for the travel and 72-68 after the free throw.

The NYT says Syracuse was within two with 4:25 left and that UConn began its free-throw parade 'with a 2-point lead' in the last 3:09; exact scores at those moments were not found, so they are not beats.
Who scored Syracuse's points from 68 to 75 in the final 30 seconds is not identified.

Clock for the 57-57 tie is approximate ('about 8 1/2 minutes' per the Washington Post); the 10-0 start and the 17-5 score are also approximate ('first four minutes', 'six minutes into' / 'with 14 minutes left').
The Herald's 'Walker emerges' sidebar says Walker played 24 minutes; the AP box has no minutes. NYT gives Gwynn 12 minutes and Sellers 2.
The NYT (March 13) quotes Oliver Macklin's sister saying he played 5.2 seconds; Macklin does not appear in the AP box. Not used.
The LA Times called this UConn's 'first tournament berth since 1978'; the record book shows UConn's previous NCAA appearance was in the 1978-79 season (March 1979). Not used.
The 74-70 beat at 0:19.4 comes only from a CBS on-screen graphic in the YouTube broadcast.
